text:
The gain error comes from the feedback network. For this non-inverting stage, the closed-loop gain is 1 + Rf/Rg = 1 + 1227/2528.2 ≈ 1.485, and the simulated 1.458 is consistent with that once finite open-loop gain is included. The 0.9–1.1 V/V window therefore requires a much smaller Rf/Rg ratio, so one of the two feedback resistors is the corrupted element. Bandwidth, power, and offset all pass, which points away from the op-amp core and the compensation network.

Rg is the most likely culprit. Its value, 2528.2 Ω, is an odd-looking figure compared with the round values elsewhere, which suggests it was altered. Rf is second. The third candidate is Cc, though its bandwidth and phase effects are not obviously consistent with the passing bandwidth spec.
